summary: Steam is a heavier train pick-up-and-deliver game where players build track networks, then run trains to fulfill goods deliveries for income or victory points. It rewards careful route planning and timing of upgrades, with tense decisions about spending on infrastructure versus banking points.
praised: Good player interaction over shared track and goods
criticised: Can feel fiddly with cubes and cards
Some find the theme thin compared to the mechanics

interaction.detail: Players compete for the same track spaces, cities, and goods cubes on a shared board, so building into contested areas or grabbing high-value goods directly affects opponents' options. Turn order is auctioned, adding another layer of direct interaction each round.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Victory points come primarily from delivering goods along built track, converted from income at round's end.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by efficiently building track and delivering goods to score the most victory points over the course of the game.
